Subject: Re: Post-call — perf targets & streaming needs

Thanks for the call earlier. Summarizing Acme's priority items so we have a clean mutual action plan: 

- Latency goal: 95th percentile <= 220ms for single-turn product search prompts (avg prompt length ~60 tokens).
- Streaming use case: multi-part conversational walkthroughs (server -> client streaming required for token-by-token display). Target tail latency 300ms for first token, steady-state token interval <= 40ms.
- Throughput: peak 3,000 QPS during flash sales, sustained 600 QPS baseline.
- Concurrency: expected 12k concurrent user sessions (KV per session), but active model concurrency estimated ~1,200.
- Cache expectations: significant prefix reuse for product titles — want to understand caching hit % we can expect and how that affects cost.

Immediate asks from Acme:
1) Can you provide an expected cost range for hitting the latency targets with and without aggressive prefix caching?
2) What model variants / quantized profiles would you recommend to keep the 95p latency target under 220ms?
3) Any constraints on streaming support (SDKs, chunk sizes, connection lifecycle) that we should design for now?

Attaching our quick MAP spreadsheet for alignment. Can we aim to lock the mutual plan and decision owners by EOD Thursday?

— Lindsey
Head of Conversational Products
Acme Retail

Appending a few concrete levers from the runtime side and an initial hypothesis for cost impact: 

Runtime levers to hit 95p <= 220ms:
- Continuous batching window: tighten to 10ms for low-latency paths; accept slightly lower throughput efficiency. (Good for first-token latency)
- KV/prefix caching: target 60–70% hit rate for product title prefixes; cache at route edge with 512MB per worker to minimize KV fetches.
- Quantization: INT8/INT4 profiles look promising — INT8 alpha should hit latency targets for our M-size variants with minimal quality loss; INT4 may need accuracy checks against your prompt set.
- Model routing: warm-path routing to a smaller distilled variant for high-frequency short prompts; full-size model as fallback for long tail.

Estimated cost sensitivity (very rough):
- Baseline (no caching, INT8): $0.82 / 1k token-equivalent requests at 600 QPS sustained.
- With prefix caching (60% hit) + INT8: $0.46 / 1k.
- Aggressive batching (larger window) reduces cost but increases tail latency; not recommended for your 95p target.

I'll run an on-prem microbench this afternoon and drop sample latency traces into the shared Drive (latency-sample-traces.txt). We'll validate the INT4 profile tomorrow with Marissa running the eval set.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
